'''Malique Lewis''' (born 10 November 2004) is a Trinidadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).

==Early life==
Lewis was born in [[Trinidad and Tobago]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Malique Lewis |url=https://www.acb.com/jugador/temporada-a-temporada/id/30001261 |website=acb.com |access-date=23 April 2025 |language=es}}</ref> His hometown is [[San Fernando, Trinidad and Tobago|San Fernando]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Get to Know Your New NBL25 Phoenix Players: Malique Lewis |url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/get-to-know-your-new-nbl25-phoenix-players-malique-lewis |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=South East Melbourne Phoenix {{!}} Official NBL Website |date=20 July 2024}}</ref> He grew up playing [[Association football|football]] until picking up basketball during his teenage years.<ref name=declares>{{cite news |title=Next Star takes step towards NBA goal |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/next-star-takes-step-towards-nba-goal |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=NBL.com.au |date=23 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
As a 16-year-old, Lewis moved to Spain to play for [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]] in the [[Liga ACB]], where he went up from 2.3 minutes in three appearances during the [[2021–22 ACB season|2021–22 season]] to 19 games in [[2022–23 ACB season|2022–23]] for almost 18 minutes per game and 4.8 points and 3.5 rebounds.<ref name="declares" /> In May 2023, he produced the fourth-highest scoring game in ACB history by a player aged 18 or younger with 24 points against [[Obradoiro CAB|Obradoiro]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Next Star Malique Lewis Signs with Phoenix |url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/next-star-malique-lewis-signs-with-phoenix |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=South East Melbourne Phoenix {{!}} Official NBL Website |date=11 July 2024}}</ref>

Lewis joined the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]] for the [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–24 season]], where he played in 50 games and averaged 8.3 points and 5.8 rebounds in over 25 minutes per game.<ref name="declares" />

In July 2024, Lewis signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) as part of the league's ''Next Stars'' program.<ref>{{cite news |title=NBA draft prospect Lewis joins NBL's Phoenix |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/40535473/nba-draft-prospect-malique-lewis-joins-nbl-phoenix |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=11 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Jackson |first1=Andrew |title='Tremendous upside': {{sic|Car|ribean|nolink=yes}} NBA prospect Malique Lewis unveiled as latest NBL Next Star |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-2024-malique-lewis-signs-with-south-east-melbourne-phoenix-next-stars-program-full-list-of-nbl-next-stars-for-202425-season/news-story/74bbfbb62426b261157efe25e425035b |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=foxsports.com.au |date=11 July 2024}}</ref> He became an important piece for the Phoenix over the course of the [[2024–25 NBL season|2024–25 season]], becoming one of the premier defenders on the team.<ref name=rookieme>{{cite news |last1=Badkin |first1=Liam |title=NBL25 Next Star review - Malique Lewis |url=https://central.rookieme.com/basketball/nbl25-next-star-review-malique-lewis/ |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=Basketball Rookie Me Central |date=11 March 2025}}</ref> He scored a season-high 15 points in November 2024, and for the season averaged 6.8 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.<ref name="rookieme" />

In April 2025, Lewis declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]].<ref name="declares" /><ref>{{cite news |title=NBL Next Stars declare for 2025 NBA Draft {{!}} Basketball.com.au |url=https://www.basketball.com.au/news/nbl-next-stars-izan-almansa-and-malique-lewis-declare-for-2025-nba-draft |access-date=23 April 2025 |work=www.basketball.com.au |date=23 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref> On 11 June 2025, he withdrew his name from the draft and subsequently returned to the South East Melbourne Phoenix for the [[2025–26 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Next stop, NBL26: Lewis runs it back with Phoenix |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/next-stop-nbl26-lewis-runs-it-back-with-phoenix |access-date=11 June 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=11 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref> On 6 November 2025, he scored a career-high 23 points in a 103–102 win over the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Phoenix prevail in Launceston shootout |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/phoenix-prevail-in-launceston-shootout |access-date=8 November 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=6 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Badkin |first1=Liam |title=Lewis makes the leap in breakout performance |url=https://central.rookieme.com/basketball/lewis-makes-the-leap-in-breakout-performance/ |access-date=8 November 2025 |work=Basketball Rookie Me Central |date=7 November 2025}}</ref> Later that month, he began suffering from [[pneumothorax]], a condition that the affects lungs.<ref>{{cite news |title=United star's new setback; Tassie sweat on skipper's season — NBL Casualty Ward |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-2025-latest-injury-and-team-news-casualty-ward-shea-ili-suffers-setback-will-magnay/news-story/21ea288d98c6960f6dbe2d64a06f2d05 |access-date=26 December 2025 |work=Fox Sports |date=21 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He missed a month of action due to pneumothorax and a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=DREWITT'S BULBS MATCH PREVIEW: Phoenix head to Hobart after nine-day break |url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/drewitts-bulbs-match-preview-phoenix-head-to-hobart-after-nine-day-break |access-date=30 December 2025 |work=South East Melbourne Phoenix {{!}} Official NBL Website |date=28 December 2025}}</ref>
